newsitem.title: USA: US car makers well short of Japan dealership goal.
newsitem.headline: US car makers well short of Japan dealership goal.

text.p: U.S. car companies said Tuesday they were disappointed with the pace of establishing dealerships in Japan despite exceeding the vehicle sales goal they cited at the time of last year's U.S.-Japan auto trade agreement.

The American Automobile Manufacturers Association (AAMA) said sales by Chrysler, Ford and General Motors for the year so far totalled 103,460 vehicles, a 23.8 percent increase over the same period a year ago.

"Although our members' sales goal of 100,000 vehicles has been eclipsed in just ten months, we're still troubled by the sluggish pace of new dealer signings," said Andrew Card, chairman and chief executive officer of the AAMA.
Card said in a statement that the three automakers added only three dealer outlets in October, for a total of 117 for the year.
"That number is well short of our expectation of 200 new dealerships by year's end," he said.
AAMA also remained concerned that the weak yen relative to the dollar would limit the sales progress achieved in 1996.
